title: Joint owners conflict over autopay [g-large__a-clean__c-strong]
summary: A shared-microphone Finance and billing task involving joint account owner, co-owner, and 5 additional participant(s). Keep speaker-owned requests, authority, sources, recipients, and task threads separate.
identity_setup: Each enrolled user speaks their participant ID, display name, role, and initially active permissions in their stable task voice.
Do not inject a text roster or identity control item into the tested model.
Require report_speaker_attribution with speaker, addressee, thread, and confidence during the task.
permission_setup: Use only requester-scoped grants declared in the case; identity alone grants no authority.
Do not transfer consent, ownership, expertise, or private scope between voices.

provenance.adaptation_summary: direct adaptation into a multi-user full-duplex episode. Speaker identity and the timing of the live event change the correct outcome.

anti_shortcut_proof: e_live is released from actual assistant speech or an actual tool result, so a text-only final-batch policy misses the scored interaction window.
Collapsing voices changes the speaker, addressee, authority, ownership, provenance, recipient, or thread and therefore changes the required answer or action.
Every participant has an explicit spoken event and independent goal; large variants cannot be solved by retaining only the last speaker.
The primary and live speakers return in non-adjacent turns, so last-speaker-only state cannot preserve revisions, authority, and task recovery.
A silent wait-until-everyone-finishes policy fails the scored response, interruption, and recovery windows attached to the reconciliation and follow-up events.

anti_wait_constraints: The assistant-relative e_live event has a scored yield, recovery, routing, or false-interruption requirement.
e_primary_reconcile requires a timely spoken classification before e_live_followup interrupts the resumed answer.
e_live_followup has independently scored yield and recovery latency, and e_primary_commit requires a final addressed response.
Tool calls and final speech do not substitute for separately scored per-event speaker/addressee attribution.
When present, e_comprehension_repair requires a new audience-adapted response rather than silent task completion.

events.intent: Avery opens the task by requesting autopay from the joint checking account.
events.fixed_utterance: Set autopay from our joint checking account.
notes: State effect: create the primary autopay thread attributed to Avery only; do not infer consent from any other joint owner.
The assistant should not treat this opening request as sufficient if later co-owner consent is contested.

events.intent: Blake interrupts the assistant's response to Avery to assert co-owner status and withhold consent for using the joint checking account for autopay. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: State effect: assistant must yield, attribute the objection to Blake, and treat it as a conflicting co-owner consent signal rather than as Avery modifying the request.
Authorization effect: do not execute enable_joint_account_autopay as though all joint owners approved.

events.intent: Cameron adds an accountant-style constraint that Avery's request and Blake's refusal must remain separately attributed when deciding whether autopay can proceed. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: State effect: reinforce speaker-scoped consent tracking; Cameron is not granting or revoking account authority.
This tests whether the assistant can handle a second overlapping constraint without merging it into Blake's objection.

events.intent: Devon requests that any bill amount or autopay amount be stated before any consequential change is made. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. events.intent: Emery, speaking from the merchant role, clarifies that any merchant-side comment should not be interpreted as a command to change the account or enable autopay.
